Series::diagflat¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::diagflat() const -> Series
Series::diagflat(std::int64_t diagonal) const -> Series

What It Does¶

diagflat() flattens the input and writes those flattened values onto a diagonal of a new square matrix.

On the current verified root surface, that behavior is the same practical contract as diag_embed(): flatten first, embed second, fill everything else with zero.

So the public difference between the two names is mainly one of intent:

  • diagflat() advertises the flattening step right in the name

  • diag_embed() emphasizes the final diagonal-matrix result

Parameters¶

diagonal (std::int64_t)

The diagonal offset.

  • 0 means the main diagonal

  • positive values write above the main diagonal

  • negative values write below the main diagonal

If the flattened input has n elements, the output side length is n + abs(diagonal).

Returns¶

Series A square 2D Series containing the flattened input along one diagonal.

Gradient¶

diagflat() follows the same verified reverse-mode behavior as diag_embed(): the forward pass flattens and writes values onto one diagonal, and the reverse pass reads sensitivity back from that same diagonal.

Examples¶

Example 1. A matrix input is flattened before embedding.

std::cout << pluss::make_series({
    {1, 2},
    {3, 4},
}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64).diagflat();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=16, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0, 0, 0],
  [0, 2, 0, 0],
  [0, 0, 3, 0],
  [0, 0, 0, 4]]

Example 2. Negative offsets move the flattened values below the main diagonal.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({5, 6}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64).diagflat(-1));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 0 0 0 ⎤
⎢ 5 0 0 ⎥
⎣ 0 6 0 ⎦

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • diagflat() always flattens first on the current root surface.

  • Offsets change output size as well as diagonal position.

  • All non-diagonal entries are zero-filled.

  • Reverse-mode follows the same diagonal readback rule as diag_embed().

Summary¶

Use diagflat() when you want the flattening step to be part of the public contract of the call. If you need extraction instead of embedding, diagflat() is the wrong family entirely.

See Also¶

  • Series::diag_embed: same current value behavior under the explicit embedding name.

  • Series::diag: dual-mode extract-or-embed surface.

  • Series::diagonal: extraction-only diagonal surface.
